I've planned this as one case. Noah Patel (E1003) moved from Software Engineer to Sales Rep, effective today (2026-11-02). His Workday record already shows the new job, org, cost center and manager. His identity account and his Finance profile still reflect the old engineering role, so the plan updates both. No escalation is needed.

**What I checked:**
- **Workday:** Noah is Active as a Sales Rep in the Sales org, cost center CC-3000 Sales, reporting to Owen Iyer (E1009). Owen is an active Sales Manager. This is the only event in the feed.
- **Policy:** Old and new access may overlap for 0 days, so engineering access has to come off today, when the change takes effect.
- **Identity:** His account (`acct-e8168561`) is enabled and has All-Staff, Eng-Git and VPN-Users. A Sales Rep should get All-Staff and Sales-CRM only. Neither of those is privileged, and together they raise no segregation-of-duties conflicts. Removing VPN-Users is my call: it's in the engineering access set, and the Sales Rep set doesn't include it.
- **Finance:** His profile still says cost center CC-1000, with his old manager as expense approver. The new Workday cost center maps to CC-3000. He has no pending expense reports, so nothing needs rerouting, and no corporate card is active. The first Finance read returned a temporary "service unavailable" error, but the retry worked.

Nothing needs to change in Workday or ITSM: there's no email write-back, he isn't leaving, and he keeps his email address, licenses and mailbox.

2. **Step 2:** Removed Eng-Git and VPN-Users, and kept All-Staff. Policy allows no overlap with old access, so I removed them right away.
